item.description:
Updates stay out of your way, and Settings looks like a Mac settings window.

  • A new version waits in the panel footer as a button naming it, rather than putting a dialog in front of whatever you were doing. Portman lives in the menu bar, so that dialog usually opened behind your work, where you might never notice it.
  • Asking for an update now closes the panel first. The update window used to open underneath the panel, and you had to dismiss the panel by hand before you could read or click it.
  • Settings tabs moved up into the title bar with icons above the labels, the way macOS does it. Each tab sizes the window to its own content, so no pane ends in a band of empty space.
  • The Ignore Rules tab tells you when nothing is ignored, instead of showing an empty list four hundred points tall.

The menu bar now shows you when something needs attention, instead of waiting for you to open the panel and find it.

  • The icon takes an orange dot when a port has more than one listener, when a server has outlived the folder it came from, or when it accepts connections and then never answers.
  • Hover it and the tooltip names the problem. "Port 3000 has more than one listener" tells you what to do about it. "1 issue" does not.
  • A new problem blinks the dot twice and then settles. Nothing pulses at you all day, and it follows Reduce motion.
